scenes.heading: Triangles
scenes.say: Roofs, bridges and bike frames are built from triangles, because a triangle can't be squashed. Let's learn how to name triangles and find their missing angles.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Tear off a paper triangle's three corners
scenes.science: Side by side, they make a straight line: 180°
scenes.breaks: tearing paper only shows it works for the triangles you tried. The parallel-line reason proves it for every triangle.
scenes.say: Cut out any triangle. Tear off its three corners and line them up, points touching. They always make a straight line. That's why the angles of a triangle add to one hundred and eighty degrees. Tearing paper isn't a proof, though. Parallel lines prove it works every time.
scenes.caption: Cut out any triangle. Tear off its three corners and line them up. They always make a straight line. That's why the angles add to 180°.

scenes.heading: Names by sides
points: Isosceles: 2 equal sides, 2 equal base angles
Scalene: no equal sides or angles
scenes.say: By sides: equilateral has three equal sides, and every angle is sixty degrees. Isosceles has two equal sides and two equal base angles. Scalene has nothing equal at all.

scenes.heading: Angle sum
scenes.say: The rule: the three interior angles, a, b and c, always add to one hundred and eighty degrees.
scenes.caption: The rule: the three interior angles, a, b and c, always add to 180°.

scenes.heading: Isosceles example
scenes.question: An isosceles triangle has 40° between its equal sides. Find the base angles.
scenes.say: An isosceles triangle has forty degrees between its equal sides. The base angles are equal. Together they make one eighty minus forty, which is one hundred and forty. Halve it: each base angle is seventy degrees.
scenes.caption: An isosceles triangle has 40° between its equal sides. The base angles are equal. Together they make 180 − 40 = 140. Halve it: each base angle is 70°.

scenes.heading: Exterior angle
scenes.question: A triangle has interior angles 62° and 48°. Find the exterior angle at the third corner.
lines: Exterior = sum of the far two
scenes.say: Extend one side and you get an exterior angle. It equals the two interior angles far away from it. If they're sixty-two and forty-eight, the exterior angle is one hundred and ten degrees.
scenes.caption: Extend one side and you get an exterior angle. It equals the two far interior angles: 62 + 48 = 110°.

points: Angles in a triangle add to 180°
Exterior angle = sum of the far two
scenes.say: Quick recap. Triangle angles add to one eighty. Equilateral angles are sixty each. Isosceles base angles are equal. An exterior angle equals the far two angles added. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. Triangle angles add to 180°. Equilateral angles are 60° each. Isosceles base angles are equal. Exterior angle = the far two added. Now try the practice questions!
